## India: Regulatory & Legal Developments

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) Secretary S. Krishnan confirmed that there will be no extension for startups to meet their Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA) compliance deadlines, emphasizing the need for timely adherence. This statement underscores the government's firm stance on the Act's implementation schedule. ([Source](https://news.google.?oc=5))

The Supreme Court is currently reviewing Public Interest Litigations (PILs) that challenge the constitutionality of the DPDPA, 2023. The Court has sought responses from the Centre regarding these petitions, indicating ongoing judicial scrutiny of the new privacy framework. In a separate matter, the Supreme Court has directed MeitY to investigate a PIL concerning the recovery or destruction of Indian citizens' stolen personal data held on foreign servers. This highlights the complex challenge of data sovereignty and cross-border data breaches under the new legal regime. ([Source](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMi-?oc=5))

## India: DPDPA Implementation & Compliance

Discussions continue around the DPDPA's foundational principle of consent, with experts questioning its true cornerstone status given the Act's broader framework and permissible uses of data. A notable point of contention remains the absence of a statutory definition of "harm," which is anticipated to create interpretational uncertainties during privacy adjudication. ([Source](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihgFBVV95cUxOX29sa0lLS2N2bEpTR2RweE1hWlBkbkxZUER6Z3hBQjVuZlFhOW9YNnU1ajU2by1xN0dLc2xOeEZHblNCX2FYTTlHdDFzR1BDNEN0SG0waEZja2ZyeWRrRlh5Qlp5U0N0YnNuN2ZMTHF1Nnh5ckhYVENaVzlkN2lOY2Q2RGdHUQ?oc=5), [Source](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMioAFBVV95cUxOZHFHUHJTc0pzTzY4QmlBMS1zVWE5LVlFeTc2RV9VQk9yUWd6c25PbFlVa2owWGsyZzUzZVRlV2lvTkt0NHg1eC03NUd4eFFEWDJtZWdfQjhqdEt4SDFtaU5NSkx0UjJ6ZUhNdllKR0V2RzV1UEhXUG5ySFVub3MwYlNBWXBtWlJhMzl3NnBzbUdlR1hId20tTEtSZkU2YXA5?oc=5))

Businesses are actively navigating the DPDPA's requirements, with guidance emerging on compliance fundamentals and the anticipated DPDP Rules 2025. These rules are expected to provide more specific directives for data fiduciaries, shaping the practical application of the Act. Critical compliance deadlines for 2026-27 are now in focus, urging organizations to finalize their data protection strategies.
